chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from a man from our companions, and he was Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl, and he was nicknamed Sikbaj, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, the owner of the hostels, and he used to manage some of the affairs of the Imam (peace be upon him), who said:
He said to me one day and dictated to me from a book: 'Wearing a ring of emerald is ease, there is no difficulty in it.'

key_terms.التَّخَتُّمُ: Wearing a ring (specifically on the finger)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing an emerald ring according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam (peace be upon him) dictates to Ahmad ibn Muhammad, a trusted companion responsible for managing the Imam's affairs, that wearing an emerald ring is permissible and straightforward (*yusr*), contrasting with potential complexities or restrictions found in other traditions. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that adornment with precious stones like emeralds is not inherently prohibited but is governed by principles of modesty and avoiding extravagance, reflecting the ease (*yusr*) emphasized in Islamic jurisprudence.
